intended_scope: Lift stations, pump trains, treatment boundaries, instrumentation, SCADA-facing alerts, and maintenance evidence common in water and wastewater operations, while leaving chemistry models, compliance reporting, and full hydraulic simulation outside the scaffold.
measurement_signal_expectations: Level, flow, pressure, vibration, and water-quality observations should remain typed and quality-aware.
Telemetry comparability matters for cross-site pump and treatment analysis.
event_alarm_expectations: High-level, high-pressure, pump fault, and communication-loss contexts should remain explicit.
Alarm suppression during maintenance should remain bounded and traceable.
reliability_work_requirements: Pump or valve work should preserve verification and measurable outcome context.
Failure or recurrence context should remain available for maintenance strategy review.

safety_cyber_applicability.safety_profile_applicability: Applicable where bypass or interlock semantics affect treatment or pumping safety boundaries.
safety_cyber_applicability.cyber_profile_applicability: Applicable where remote stations, PLCs, and gateways are networked and cyber-managed.
notes: The scaffold supports foundational safety and cyber traceability only.
Water-quality regulatory semantics remain outside the core profile scaffold.

servicenow_serving_projection_implicatio: Project station status, risk, anomalies, related work, and evidence freshness rather than raw SCADA samples.
Preserve references to full SSOM evidence for maintenance and incident workflows.
known_exclusions: Detailed hydraulic model or chemistry calculation semantics.
Regulatory reporting and compliance submission formats.

end_to_end_example.scenario_label: Lift station pump degradation and workflow projection
end_to_end_example.narrative_summary: A water or wastewater pump train preserves observation, condition, work, and projection semantics so reliability risk and maintenance context remain interoperable without flattening treatment boundaries into one workflow table.

stages.summary: Flow, pressure, level, and vibration semantics remain typed and comparable.
High-level or pump-fault alarm context remains distinct from conditions and work.
Maintenance work and measurable outcome remain linked to pump recurrence evidence.
Remote station or PLC context can use bounded safety or cyber profiles where applicable.
A curated workflow projection exposes station status, risk, and related work references.
The example preserves recurrence-aware outcome semantics for asset strategy review.
